title: An in-depth visit to the Roman Forum, Palatine Hill and of course, the Colosseum
text:
Giorgia was an incredible guide, with 25 years experience as a guide in Rome. She has a wealth of knowledge and an understanding of the changes that Rome has gone through over the past 50 years, and of course, well beyond that!

The tour started up above the metro stop for the Colosseum, and although there were a lot of groups meeting there, it didn’t take long to find the group. We were given a headset to hear the guide better. We walked through the streets learning about how the Romans lived before entering the Roman Forum. There was hardly any line due to the guided tour entrance. 

I won’t spoil the fun facts I learnt along the way. You’ll need to take the tour yourself! 

After the forum, we walked through the buildings still standing around palatine hill and then went to the colosseum. There was an unavoidable line at the Colosseum, with only 3,000 people allowed in at a time. We did notice the individual line seemed to be faster than the group tour line, but it may have been the time that we entered, and many other factors. It took about 20 minutes to get into the colosseum from lining up to walking through the final ticket checkpoint. This time did give the guide opportunity to tell us about the history behind the amphitheater. The guide took us up to the level where you can see the arena and the seating areas and that’s where the tour ended.

One thing to note, I did book an 8:30am trip which was changed to a 9am but the company did communicate this very well. I was disappointed that we were entering the colosseum last (11am) as I didn’t want there to be too many people yet but in reality, ending there was better than ending at the Roman forum as it allowed us to stick around for a bit longer in the Colosseum. Note, apparently this isn’t always possible, some tour guides will need you to leave after the tour because of the max 3,000 in at one time.

Our guide, Nick, was outstanding - very knowledgeable, kept things engaging without overloading us, and managed time and logistics extremely well. He navigated the crowds at the Colosseum and kept us moving efficiently between there and Palatine Hill.

The main drawback was the meeting point. It’s above the metro station across from the Colosseum and shared by many tour companies.Its a sea of tourists with earpieces and guides in various colored shirts holding signs.  It was easy enough to find, but the exact location and - more importantly - the specific tour operator name were not clearly communicated in the emails. That should be improved.

Overall, highly recommend the tour - just make sure you have clear notes on the meeting point and operator before arriving. Thanks to Nick for a great experience.

title: Ken made Ancient Rome come alive!
text:
Our guided tour of the Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill was easily one of the highlights of our trip. While the Colosseum is impressive on its own, having a guide is absolutely essential for the Forum and Palatine Hill—without the context, you're just looking at ruins, but with a guide, you're looking at history.

Our guide, Ken, was exceptional. His passion for Roman history was evident from the moment we started. He didn't just rattle off dates and names; he told stories about the gladiators and the daily life of Romans that kept us engaged the entire three hours. He even brought along a book showcasing pictorial references of how the Colosseum and Roman Forum looked back in the day. These pictures were incredibly helpful as they allowed us to visualize exactly where we were standing in reference to the ruins today versus how they looked in their prime.

Ken also managed the group expertly, ensuring a perfect pace throughout the tour. It was steady enough to cover everything but manageable enough that my 67-year-old father could easily keep up without it being overtiring.

Highly recommend this tour, and if you get Ken, you're in for a treat!

title: Well-organized tour with knowledgeable guide, despite the crowds
text:
I joined this guided tour of the Vatican Museums in January as a solo traveler and had a very positive experience. The group was relatively small, which made it easy to follow the guide and stay engaged throughout the tour. The group itself was a mix of different travelers, including families, couples, and solo visitors, which showed that this tour is suitable for all types of travelers.

Each participant received a headset, so we could clearly hear the guide even in the extremely crowded areas. The Vatican Museums are always very busy, even in winter, so this made a big difference and helped keep the experience enjoyable.

Our guide was excellent, very knowledgeable, passionate, and engaging. She explained everything clearly and was very open to questions. She took the time to answer and interact with the group, which made the experience feel more personal and interesting.

The tour was well organized, and the entry process was smooth and efficient. Even though access to the Sistine Chapel was unexpectedly unavailable that day, the guide adapted well and showed us other important highlights of the museum. After the guided portion ended, we were free to stay inside and continue exploring on our own, which was a great advantage.

Overall, this is an excellent tour if you want a structured and informative visit to the Vatican Museums. I would highly recommend it for solo travelers, couples, and families alike.

Thank you, FI, for an unforgettable experience.

Dear Brian,

Thank you very much for taking the time to share your feedback. We’re truly sorry to hear that your experience did not fully meet your expectations.

For this reason, we were surprised by your comments regarding the audio tour. We kindly ask you to check the provider of your tour, as it appears the experience you are referring to may have been offered by a different operator.

Regarding the two-day ticket, please note that our tours do not provide two-day tickets with multiple entries. The Colosseum’s two-day ticket allows access over two days but only one entry, a rule set by the monument’s official ticketing system rather than by tour operators.

We truly appreciate your feedback, as it helps us and future travelers better understand the different ticket options available. We hope this clarifies the matter.

Kind regards,
City Walkers Team

text: I paid £217 for 2 x adults and 1 x child for the guided tour. We booked at 10am to avoid midday heat and plan the rest of our afternoon - 2 days before the tour they contacted to say the time had been changed to 11.30, with no offer to refund if we couldn't make it. My son and partner had travelled to join me in Rome for just one day so I had to go with it as I'd promised him the Colosseum. The guide seemed hassled and rushed us through everywhere as if she had better things to do, she constantly answered her phone so we could hear all her chats on the audio. She always kept checking her watch. She seemed annoyed at a few tourists not in our group, and the rush she took us through the forum was intense. We stopped only for 5 minutes for taking in the sights. I felt we looked at a rather ragged book of pictures she kept showing us rather than the actual things in front of us. The Colosseum was the last thing on the tour and we had 30minutes if that, so we stayed to explore further and she said we could use our ticket tomorrow or the day after to go back to the forum and Palatine Hill (we didn't even go down to the forum floor and we didn't go near the Palatine Hill?!). I went back the next day to look around and take in the Forum at a leisurely place and look at Palatine Hill. I was told my ticket wasn't valid, so they lied about it's validity. I checked  back with someone outside the Basilica who worked for Vivicos travel and he said it's only valid for 24 hours. I bought a new ticket for 18 euros and went back in. 18 euros, small queue, where I spent 3 + hours looking at things and listening to Rick Steves audio guide (downloadable on his app) Brilliant! Compared to £217 which was rushed and nothing looked at. She kept going on about propaganda?! We had no time to look at things.  It was a completely overpriced for 2 hours. I feel embarrassed that I fell for this and paid this much. Buy online at the official site, if available, and if not queue on the day and avoid this company and tour guides, So rushed!  My son thankfully didn't know the difference in monies spent and I shan't tell him but please save yourself £200!

title: "Top Tier Tour at The Colosseum in Rome with Alec!"
text:
As a seasoned traveller, I have been on my fair share of guided tours, and this was up there with the very best of them!

My tour guide was Alec (humourously referred to himself as Alec Baldwin to make sure people called him Alec and not Alex) and I definitely lucked out with him. I don't think you get to choose your guide, but if you get Alec, you will definitely get your money's worth.

Alec was very knowledgeable about Roman history, and also the Colosseum itself. He was thoroughly engaging, charming, and witty, making the tour fly by with this funny stories, especially about the prowess of Roman gladiators in comparison to boxing and UFC. The weather was sweltering (not unusual for central and southern Italy during July and August so bring a bottle of water) and there was a lot of walking, so get a good night's sleep the night before!

My tour included the Colosseum and the Palatine Hill - the Palatine Hill is considered the birthplace of Rome, and the total duration was around 2 hours and 15 mins. I highly recommend this tour if you are visiting Rome!

To help my fellow travellers, my top ten tips are below:

(1) Bring a bottle of water. I cannot stress how important this is. If you are coming in the summer months or early autumn, the temperatures can reach the mid to high nineties in Fahrenheit. The heat is no joke, so you need to stay hydrated. You can top up your water bottles from the drinking water points, but I cannot verify how clean the water is. Better that you fill up at the hotel before you leave or buy a bottle from a shop. Avoid buying water from the hawkers (mostly Senegalese and east african). I know they have to make a living, but you don't want to end up ill drinking contaminated water.

(2) How to get there - The Colosseum has its own Metro station. Its on the Blue Line, and its called "Colosseo". The Colosseum and the Pantheon are the two biggest landmarks in Rome, so you won't accidentally miss seeing the Colosseum. Once you exit the station, its right in front of you. To get to the meeting the point, once you have exited the barriers at the metro station, you will need to climb some stairs within the station to get to the meeting point. A lot of other tour guides congregate here, near Caffe Roma, but this tour uses light blue t shirts to identify themselves. Look for a building with  Giardino D'Infanzia inscribed in stone, with some trees in front of it. This is where the guide will get everyone together.

(3) Be On Time - Sounds simple, but to maximise the tour duration, this tour guide is big on punctuality. I suggest getting here 15 mins before the tour commences, as this allows time for the register to be taken to confirm who has arrived and who hasn't. They do not wait for latecomers. If you are late you may be able to join another tour at a later time, but I wouldn't bank on it.

(4) Bring your ID - National ID card, Drivers Licence/License or Passport only. They do rigorous checks at the start of the tour and also upon entry to the Colosseum. Digital forms of ID are acceptable. Make sure the booking is in your full government name, e.g. if your friends call you Tom, and you are Thomas, then book the tour as Thomas. They have been known to refuse entry to the Colosseum if the name on the booking, and on your ID doesn't match exactly. You have been warned!

(5) Bags are allowed, and so are rucksacks. Bring some snacks if you want with your water and also some sunscreen. Once you enter the Colosseum, there is a metal detector and baggage scanner that you have to put your bag through for security purposes.

(6) Wear comfortable footwear. Don't wear boots. Sandals or soft soled sneakers/trainers are advised. You will definitely do more than 10000 steps. Bring your step counter watch if you don't believe me!

(7) Toilets are only at the entrance inside the Colosseum, and it gets busy. Once you past the entrance, there will be no opportunity for a toilet break for the remainder of the tour. The toilets are not the cleanest, so empty your bladder at the hotel before you come to the Colosseum, if possible.

(8) Pick a time slot between 8:30am and 10:30am. The Colosseum gets very, very crowded, very, very quickly, especially during peak season. Most visitors were British, American, Australian or Canadian, from the accents that I heard. Beware of pickpockets, keep your phone and valuables in your FRONT pockets or in your bag. Consider padlocking the main compartment of your bag/rucksack as well.

(9) Tips aren't compulsory, American visitors are used to tipping in the USA, but as a born and bred Londoner and regular European traveller, tips aren't really a thing on this side of the pond, in the UK, France, Italy, Spain, etc. Feel free to tip if you do get good service though. 5 euros is the sweet spot if you are feeling generous. 

(10) Last tip - take LOTS of photographs. Charge up your phone and take as many selfies as you want. People are friendly enough to take pictures of you and your family/husband/wife as long as you ask politely. Who wouldn't want to come to Rome and not get a picture in front of the Colosseum!

HAVE FUN!!
